copy.bis: Gigamit ang optical fibers aron susihon ang mga mechanical weld sa tubo ug makina, nga makatabang sa mga engineer nga makita ang depekto nga dili ablihan ang mga parte.

copy.bis: Adunay mga egret ug heron nga moabot sa Pilipinas gikan sa layong nasod panahon sa tingtugnaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because wetland soil is super full of water, very little oxygen can reach all the way down to the roots!

Because wetland soil is super full of water, very little oxygen can reach all the way down to the roots!

Dahil punong-puno ng tubig ang lupa ng wetland, kakaunti lang ang hanging-oxygen na nakaaabot pababa sa mga ugat!
copy.bis:
Ngano gamay ra kaayo ang oxygen sa yuta sa wetland?

Tungod kay ang yuta sa wetland puno kaayo sa tubig, gamay ra kaayo ang oxygen nga makaabot pailawom sa mga gamot!

copy.tl: Ang ilang balyena ay naglalakbay ng libo-libong kilometro bawat taon sa pagitan ng malamig na tubig kung saan sila kumakain at mainit na tubig kung saan sila nanganganak, sinusundan ang parehong ruta taon-taon.
copy.bis: Ang pipila ka balyena mopanaw og liboan ka kilometro matag tuig taliwala sa bugnaw nga tubig diin sila mokaon ug init nga tubig diin sila manganak, gisubay ang samang ruta matag tuig.

What does the giant whale shark eat?

Even though it's huge, the whale shark eats only plankton and tiny fish, filtering them out of the water.
copy.tl:
Ano ang kinakain ng malaking butanding?

Kahit napakalaki nito, ang butanding ay kumakain lamang ng plankton at maliliit na isda sa pamamagitan ng pagsala ng tubig.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gikaon sa dakong tuki?

Bisan pa sa iyang kadako, ang tuki mokaon lang og plankton ug gagmayng isda pinaagi sa pagsala sa tubig.

What is the largest fish in the world?

The whale shark (Rhincodon typus) is the largest fish species in the world.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking isda sa mundo?

Ang butanding o whale shark (Rhincodon typus) ang pinakamalaking isda sa mundo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga isda sa kalibutan?

Ang butanding o whale shark (Rhincodon typus) mao ang pinakadako nga isda sa kalibutan.

How do scientists tell whale sharks apart?

Each whale shark has a unique pattern of white spots — scientists use pattern-recognition software on photos to identify them, just like human fingerprints.
copy.tl:
Paano nakikilala ng siyentipiko ang bawat whale shark?

Ang bawat whale shark ay may natatanging disenyo ng puting spot — ginagamit ng mga siyentipiko ang pattern recognition software sa mga litrato para matukoy ito, tulad ng fingerprint ng tao.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-ila sa siyentipiko sa matag whale shark?

Ang matag whale shark adunay natatanging disenyo sa puting spot — ang mga siyentipiko naggamit sa pattern recognition software sa mga litrato aron mailhan kini, sama sa fingerprint sa tawo.

copy.en: Many tourists go to Donsol just to see whale sharks — and that gives jobs to the local people there!
copy.tl: Maraming turista ang pumupunta sa Donsol para makita ang butanding — at ito ay nagbibigay ng trabaho sa mga taga-roon!
copy.bis: Daghang turista moadto sa Donsol aron makita ang butanding — ug kini naghatag og trabaho sa mga lumad didto!

copy.bis: Ang mineral usa ka natural nga solidong butang nga adunay piho nga kemikal ug kasagaran adunay porma sa kristal. Mga mineral ang hinimo sa bato!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to discuss the regular occurrence of meteor showers
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single meteor (shooting star) and does not discuss meteor showers, their regular occurrence, or gathering information from secondary sources. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: A 'shooting star' is not really a star! It's a tiny space rock burning up from friction as it races through Earth's air — making a bright streak of light!
copy.tl: Ang 'shooting star' o bulalakaw ay hindi talaga bituin! Maliit na bato ito mula sa kalawakan na nasusunog dahil sa friction habang humahagibis sa hangin ng Earth — kaya may guhit ng liwanag!
copy.bis: Ang 'shooting star' o bulalakaw dili gyud bituon! Gamayng bato kini gikan sa kawanangan nga nasunog tungod sa friction samtang naghaguros sa hangin sa Earth — maong adunay guhit nga kahayag!

In what year was the planet Neptune discovered?

The beautiful planet Neptune was officially discovered in the year 1846!

Kailan natuklasan ang planetang Neptune?

Natuklasan ang planetang Neptune noong taong 1846!
copy.bis:
Kanus-a nadiskobre ang planetang Neptune?

Nadiskobre ang planetang Neptune niadtong tuig 1846!

The amazing planet Uranus was discovered a long time ago, in the exact year 1781!
copy.tl:
Kailan natuklasan ang planetang Uranus?

Ang planetang Uranus ay natuklasan noong taong 1781!
copy.bis:
Kanus-a nadiskobre ang planetang Uranus?

Ang planetang Uranus nadiskobre niadtong tuig 1781!

copy.tl: Ang whipworm ay isang manipis at palihim na bulate na naninirahan sa malaking bituka at maaaring magdulot ng madalas na pagtatae.
copy.bis: Ang whipworm usa ka nipis ug tago nga bulate nga nagpuyo sa dakong tinai ug makahatag og subsob nga kalibang.

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that white sand comes from crushed coral and shells, which is about the origin of sand from biological materials, not about how soil is formed from rocks and minerals. It shares the broad earth-materials topic but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The beautiful white sand of islands like Boracay comes from crushed coral and shells!
copy.tl: Ang puting buhangin sa mga isla tulad ng Boracay ay galing sa durog na bahura at kabibe!
copy.bis: Ang puti nga balas sa mga isla sama sa Boracay naggikan sa dugmok nga bahura ug kabhang!

copy.en:
Who discovered Pluto?

An astronomer named Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto!
copy.tl:
Sino ang nakatuklas ng Pluto?

Si Clyde Tombaugh ang nakatuklas ng Pluto!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang nakadiskobre sa Pluto?

Si Clyde Tombaugh ang nakadiskobre sa Pluto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brown spots appear because the banana's starch is turning into sugar!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brown spots appear because the banana's starch is turning into sugar!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible

copy.en:
Why do brown spots appear on a ripening banana?

Brown spots appear because the banana's starch is turning into sugar! That is why a banana with many dark spots tastes much sweeter.
copy.tl:
Bakit lumalabas ang kayumangging mantsa sa hinihinog na saging?

Lumalabas ang mantsa dahil nagiging asukal ang almirol ng saging! Kaya mas matamis ang saging na maraming itim na mantsa.
copy.bis:
Nganong mogawas ang brown nga mga puntik sa saging nga mohinog?

Mogawas ang puntik kay ang almirol sa saging nahimong kalamay! Mao nga mas tam-is ang saging nga daghan og itom nga puntik.

assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on the circulatory and digestive systems but does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. It only gives a single physiological response without explaining system function.

copy.en:
Why do we feel 'butterflies' when nervous?

When we're nervous, the body releases a chemical that readies us to 'fight or flee,' and it reduces blood flow to the stomach — giving us that fluttering feeling inside!
copy.tl:
Bakit may 'paru-paro' sa tiyan kapag kinakabahan?

Kapag kinakabahan tayo, naglalabas ang katawan ng kemikal na naghahanda sa atin sa 'laban o takbo,' at binabawasan nito ang daloy ng dugo sa tiyan — kaya nararamdaman natin ang kakaibang kabog sa loob!
copy.bis:
Nganong naay 'alibangbang' sa tiyan kon kulbaan?

Kon kulbaan ta, ang lawas mopagawas og kemikal nga mag-andam nato sa 'pakig-away o pagdagan,' ug makunhoran niini ang dagan sa dugo sa tiyan — mao nga mabati nato ang lahi nga pagkurog sa sulod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scientists think the nervous system controls this to help us grip wet things better
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a possible adaptive function (better grip) but does not describe how an animal has changed over time to suit its environment, nor does it use secondary sources to present an example like mimicry or camouflage. The wrinkling is a temporary physiological response, not an evolutionary adaptation.

copy.en:
Why do your fingers wrinkle in water?

When we stay in water a long time, our finger skin wrinkles — scientists think the nervous system controls this to help us grip wet things better!
copy.tl:
Bakit nagkukulubot ang daliri sa tubig?

Kapag matagal tayo sa tubig, kumukulubot ang balat ng ating mga daliri — pinaniniwalaang kontrolado ito ng nervous system para mas mahigpit tayong makahawak ng basang bagay!
copy.bis:
Nganong mokunot ang tudlo sa tubig?

Kon dugay ta sa tubig, mokunot ang panit sa atong mga tudlo — gituohan nga gikontrol kini sa nervous system aron mas lig-on tang makagunit og basa nga butang!

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the length of a year and the leap-year calendar adjustment, which relates to Earth's orbit but does not involve a Sun-Earth-Moon model, seasons, star patterns, or eclipses as required by the competency.

copy.en: A year is about 365 and a quarter days, Earth's orbit time. Every 4 years, we add February 29 to keep the calendar lined up. That's a leap year!
copy.tl: Ang isang taon ay halos 365 at kalahating-kapat na araw, ang oras na iniikot ng Earth. Tuwing 4 na taon, nagdadagdag tayo ng February 29 para sa leap year!
copy.bis: Ang usa ka tuig halos 365 ug tunga-kuwarto ka adlaw, ang panahon nga libuton sa Earth. Matag 4 ka tuig, magdugang tag February 29 aron magpabiling sakto ang leap year!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You cry less if you chill the onion first or use a sharp knife!

It does not explain factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions, nor does it connect to food preservation, materials production, control of fire, pollution, or corrosion as required by G10-M-8. The content is only tangentially related to chemistry (tear-causing gas) and does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: You cry less if you chill the onion first or use a sharp knife! Fewer cells are torn, so less tear-causing gas escapes from the onion.
copy.tl: Mas kaunti ang luha kapag pinalamig muna ang sibuyas o gumamit ng matalim na kutsilyo! Mas konting selula ang nasisira, kaya mas kaunting gas ang lumalabas.
copy.bis: Mas gamay ang luha kung bugnawon una ang sibuyas o mogamit og hait nga kutsilyo! Mas gamay ang nadaot nga selula, busa mas gamay ang gas nga mogawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines is tropical because it sits near the equator, where the sun's heat is strongest!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains tropical climate by proximity to the equator and strong sunlight, but does not mention Earth's tilt, its orbit, or how tilt affects sunlight intensity over a year, nor does it use a model or drawings as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that the Philippines has no winter and stays warm all year, which touches on seasons, but it does not describe the different seasons in the Philippines or suggest activities appropriate for each season as the competency requires.

copy.en: The Philippines is tropical because it sits near the equator, where the sun's heat is strongest! That's why it stays warm all year round and has no winter.
copy.tl: Tropikal ang Pilipinas dahil nasa malapit sa equator, kung saan pinakamatindi ang init ng araw! Kaya mainit tayo buong taon at walang winter.
copy.bis: Tropikal ang Pilipinas kay naa kini duol sa equator, diin pinakakusog ang init sa adlaw! Maong init kita tibuok tuig ug walay winter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its molecules are packed tightly with no gaps
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use diagrams and illustrations to describe the arrangement, spacing, and relative motion of the particles in each of the three states (phases) of matter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions tight packing of molecules, which touches on particle arrangement, but it does not use diagrams or illustrations and does not describe arrangement, spacing, and relative motion across the three states of matter. It only gives a single fact about rubber as a solid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rubber blocks water because its molecules are packed tightly with no gaps
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about rubber being waterproof, not about describing physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. Waterproofness is not one of the listed physical properties, so the card does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: Rubber blocks water because its molecules are packed tightly with no gaps! That is why it is perfect for raincoats, boots, and seals to keep you dry.
copy.tl: Tinatanggal ng goma ang tubig dahil siksik ang mga molecules niya at walang gaps! Kaya perfect ito sa mga kapote, bota, at selyo para manatiling tuyo.
copy.bis: Gibloke sa goma ang tubig tungod kay hugot ang pagkasumpay sa molecules niini ug walay gaps! Mao nga perfect kini sa mga kapote, botas, ug selyo aron magpabiling uga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's all about melanin, a natural pigment! More melanin means darker skin and stronger protection from the sun.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions variation in skin color but does not discuss evolution concepts such as heredity, isolation, selection, or adaptation. It provides no instructional support for discussing theories of evolution.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's all about melanin, a natural pigment! More melanin means darker skin and stronger protection from the sun.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions melanin as a pigment but does not explain the role of DNA, genes, or chromosomes in the transmission of traits. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why do people have different skin colors?

It's all about melanin, a natural pigment! More melanin means darker skin and stronger protection from the sun. Every skin color is normal and good.
copy.tl:
Bakit iba-iba ang kulay ng balat?

Dahil ito sa melanin, isang likas na pigment! Mas maraming melanin, mas maitim ang balat at mas malakas ang proteksyon laban sa araw. Lahat ng kulay ng balat ay normal at maganda.
copy.bis:
Ngano lain-lain ang kolor sa panit?

Tungod kini sa melanin, usa ka natural nga pigment! Mas daghang melanin, mas itom ang panit ug mas kusgan ang panalipod batok sa adlaw. Tanang kolor sa panit normal ug nindot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They make acid as the flour ferments, giving it that sour taste.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify the products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g. cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why sourdough bread is sour, mentioning fermentation and acid production by bacteria. It does not identify products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g., cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco) as required by the competency. The content is only tangentially related to fermentation and does not directly support the skill of identifying such products.

copy.en:
Why is sourdough bread sour?

The dough holds helpful bacteria alongside yeast! They make acid as the flour ferments, giving it that sour taste.
copy.tl:
Bakit maasim ang sourdough bread?

May mga mabubuting bakterya sa masa kasama ng lebadura! Gumagawa sila ng acid habang nagfe-ferment ang harina, kaya nagiging maasim.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga aslom ang sourdough bread?

Adunay maayong bakterya sa masa uban sa lebadura! Mobuhat sila og acid samtang nag-ferment ang harina, mao nga aslom kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body's way of warning you about possibly poisonous plants
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why bitter substances taste bitter as a warning against poisonous plants, but it does not explain how interactions between living things or between living and non-living things bring good or harm. The mention of poisonous plants is a tangential connection, not instruction on the competency's core concept of interaction outcomes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your tongue senses as bitter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the tongue sensing bitterness, which touches on a sensory function, but it does not describe how any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) works. It is not instructional for the competency.

copy.en:
Why do coffee and bitter melon taste so bitter?

They contain substances your tongue senses as bitter — your body's way of warning you about possibly poisonous plants!
copy.tl:
Bakit mapait ang kape at ampalaya?

May mga sangkap sila na nararamdaman ng dila bilang pait — paraan ng katawan para mag-ingat sa mga posibleng nakakalasong halaman!
copy.bis:
Ngano pait ang kape ug paliya?

Adunay mga sustansya sila nga mabati sa dila isip pait — paagi sa lawas aron mag-amping sa mga tanom nga posibleng makahilo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To spread tears that clean and moisten our eyes, and to protect them from dust and bright light!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the function of blinking (spreading tears, protection) but does not describe outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement and food gathering. The eye is an outer body part, but the card does not teach the competency's specific content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To spread tears that clean and moisten our eyes, and to protect them from dust and bright light!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a protective/cleaning function of blinking, not the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Blinking is a response, but the card does not describe it as a characteristic of living things or address growth or reproduction.

copy.en:
Why do we blink?

To spread tears that clean and moisten our eyes, and to protect them from dust and bright light!
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo kumukurap?

Para ikalat ang luha na naglilinis at nagpapabasa sa mata natin, at para protektahan ito sa alikabok at sobrang liwanag!
copy.bis:
Nganong mokurap kita?

Aron ikatag ang luha nga maglimpyo ug magpabasa sa atong mata, ug aron panalipdan kini gikan sa abog ug sobra nga kahayag!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Eyebrows keep sweat and rain from running into our eyes, while eyelashes catch dust before it gets in.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes human eyebrows and eyelashes as protective outer body parts, but the competency requires identifying roles of animal outer body parts for movement and food gathering. The card does not address movement or food gathering, so it only shares the broad topic of body parts.

copy.en:
Why do we have eyebrows and eyelashes?

Eyebrows keep sweat and rain from running into our eyes, while eyelashes catch dust before it gets in. Both protect our eyesight!
copy.tl:
Bakit meron tayong kilay at pilikmata?

Pumipigil ang kilay sa pawis at ulan na tumulo sa mata, habang sumasalo naman ang pilikmata sa alikabok bago ito makapasok. Pareho silang nagpoprotekta sa paningin!
copy.bis:
Ngano naa tay kilay ug pilok?

Ang kilay nagpugong sa singot ug ulan nga modiretso sa mata, samtang ang pilok mosalo sa abog una kini makasulod. Pareho silang nanalipod sa panan-aw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We pee to get rid of waste and extra water from our body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a basic fact about excretion (peeing removes waste) but does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together. It only touches the topic of excretion without supporting the competency's required representation or systems-integration skill.

copy.en:
Why do we pee?

We pee to get rid of waste and extra water from our body — stuff that could harm us if it stayed inside.
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo umiihi?

Umiihi tayo para alisin ang dumi at sobrang tubig sa katawan — mga bagay na puwedeng makasama kung mananatili sa loob.
copy.bis:
Ngano ta mangihi?

Mangihi ta aron kuhaon ang hugaw ug sobra nga tubig sa lawas — mga butang nga makadaot kon magpabilin sulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because of a natural gel called mucilage inside its leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses mucilage, a gel inside leaves, not a specialized plant structure such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. It does not describe the purpose of any specialized structure, so it only shares the broad plant topic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because of a natural gel called mucilage inside its leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves but does not describe observing outer parts of plants or their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It explains sliminess from mucilage, which is not the role of leaves as described in the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because of a natural gel called mucilage inside its leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a gel (mucilage) that makes cooked saluyot slimy, but this is not a physical property of a solid material like hard, shiny, or stretchable. The slimy texture is a property of a cooked plant substance, not a solid material property as required.

copy.en:
Why does cooked saluyot get slimy?

Because of a natural gel called mucilage inside its leaves — the same substance that thickens okra. It's not dirt, it's really part of the plant.
copy.tl:
Bakit malagkit ang saluyot pag niluto?

Dahil sa likas na gel na tinatawag mucilage sa loob ng dahon — ito rin ang nagpapalapot sa okra. Hindi ito dumi, bahagi talaga ito ng halaman.
copy.bis:
Nganong madanlog ang saluyot kung lutoon?

Tungod sa natural nga gel nga gitawag mucilage sa sulod sa dahon — mao usab kini ang nagpabaga sa okra. Dili kini hugaw, bahin gyud kini sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind is the main shaper! Since there are few plants or water to hold the soil, wind blows and shapes the desert.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes wind as a shaper of desert land, which is a form of erosion, but it does not demonstrate or explain how erosion transports Earth materials. The competency specifically requires demonstrating transport of materials, which is not addressed.

copy.en:
What shapes the land in deserts?

Wind is the main shaper! Since there are few plants or water to hold the soil, wind blows and shapes the desert.
copy.tl:
Ano ang humuhubog sa lupa sa mga disyerto?

Ang hangin ang pangunahing humuhubog! Dahil kakaunti ang halaman at tubig na humahawak sa lupa, hangin ang bumabagyo at humuhubog sa disyerto.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghulma sa yuta sa mga disyerto?

Ang hangin ang nag-unang naghulma! Kay gamay ra ang tanom ug tubig nga mihupot sa yuta, hangin ang mohulma sa disyerto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Together they make a large amount of electricity.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a group of wind turbines (a wind farm) produces a large amount of electricity. It does not address evaluating renewable/non-renewable generation in the Philippines, nor impacts on human activities and the environment, nor gathering information from secondary sources.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Together they make a large amount of electricity.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions electricity generation by wind turbines but does not describe high voltage generation, safe distribution, substations, grid stations, or electric meters. It does not support the specific competency content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Together they make a large amount of electricity.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies wind turbines as a source of electricity, but the competency focuses on observing and identifying sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, home, and community. Electricity is not one of the listed energy forms, and the card does not address light, sound, or heat.

copy.en:
What do you call a group of wind turbines?

A wind farm! Together they make a large amount of electricity.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa maraming turbina na magkakatabi?

Wind farm! Sama-sama silang gumagawa ng maraming kuryente.
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag sa daghang turbine nga magkatapok?

Wind farm! Dungan sila nga maghimo og daghang kuryente.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the morning, air rises up slopes as a valley breeze! At night, cooler air flows down as a mountain breeze.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes valley and mountain breezes, which are thermally driven winds, but the competency specifically requires explaining how solar energy contributes to land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the ITCZ. The card does not address any of those named phenomena, so it only shares the broad topic of solar-driven breezes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the morning, air rises up slopes as a valley breeze! At night, cooler air flows down as a mountain breeze.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies solar heating causes air to rise up slopes, but it does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere in general. It focuses on a specific local breeze pattern rather than the broader atmospheric interaction required by the competency.

copy.en:
Ever wonder how wind moves in the mountains?

In the morning, air rises up slopes as a valley breeze! At night, cooler air flows down as a mountain breeze.
copy.tl:
Napapansin mo ba kung paano gumagalaw ang hangin sa bundok?

Sa umaga, umakyat ang hangin bilang valley breeze! Sa gabi naman, bumababa ang mas malamig na hangin bilang mountain breeze.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba ka unsaon paglihok sa hangin sa bukid?

Sa buntag, mosaka ang hangin isip valley breeze! Sa gabii, manaog ang mas mabugnaw nga hangin isip mountain breeze.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The electricity made by a turbine flows through wires straight to your homes and buildings!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that electricity from a turbine flows through wires to homes/buildings. It does not describe high-voltage generation, safe distribution, substations/grid stations, or electric meters, which are the core requirements of G10-F-9. The statement is a simplified, general fact about electricity distribution, not direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The electricity made by a turbine flows through wires straight to your homes and buildings!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions electricity flowing through wires but does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons, nor does it address safe measures in handling electricity. It is only tangentially related to the concept of electric current, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en: The electricity made by a turbine flows through wires straight to your homes and buildings!
copy.tl: Ang kuryenteng gawa ng turbina ay dumadaloy sa mga kable papunta sa mga bahay at gusali!
copy.bis: Ang kuryente nga hinimo sa turbine moagi sa mga kable padulong sa mga balay ug building!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Trade winds are steady winds blowing from 30° north and south toward the equator!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes trade winds, a global wind pattern, but does not explain how solar energy contributes to land and sea breezes, monsoons, or the ITCZ. Trade winds are not one of the named phenomena in the competency, and the card lacks any causal link to solar energy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Trade winds are steady winds blowing from 30° north and south toward the equator!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions wind direction (blowing toward the equator) but does not identify or describe basic weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, humidity, rain, or cloud cover. It only gives a single fact about a specific wind pattern, not a general description of weather characteristics.

copy.en:
What are trade winds?

Trade winds are steady winds blowing from 30° north and south toward the equator! Long ago, sailing ships used them to cross the ocean.
copy.tl:
Ano ang trade winds?

Ang trade winds ay matatag na hangin na hinihip mula 30° hilaga at timog patungo sa ekwador! Noon, ginamit sila ng mga barkong may layag para tumawid sa karagatan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang trade winds?

Ang trade winds matatag nga mga hangin nga mohuyop gikan sa 30° amihanan ug habagat padulong sa ekwador! Kaniadto, gigamit kini sa mga barkong de layag aron motabok sa dagat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its long wings make lift as it slowly descends.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses glider flight and lift, not gravity as a non-contact force. The slow descent is an implicit effect of gravity, but the card does not identify or explain gravity's role, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its long wings make lift as it slowly descends.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the glider slowly descending, which is a motion affected by gravity, but it does not observe or describe the effects of gravity on the object's motion. The focus is on lift and flight, not on gravity's influence.

copy.en: A glider has no engine but still flies! Its long wings make lift as it slowly descends.
copy.tl: Ang glider ay walang makina ngunit nakakalipad pa rin! Ang mahaba nitong pakpak ay gumagawa ng lift habang dahan-dahang bumababa.
copy.bis: Ang glider walay makina apan makalupad gihapon! Ang taas niini nga pako naghimo og lift samtang hinay-hinay nga mokanaog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If the wing tilts too steeply, air stops flowing smoothly and lift suddenly drops.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a stall in terms of airflow and lift, but does not mention balanced or unbalanced forces, nor provide examples of everyday situations demonstrating these force concepts. It shares the broad topic of forces but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If the wing tilts too steeply, air stops flowing smoothly and lift suddenly drops.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate in practical situations and describe that acceleration is a change in speed and/or direction as the result of a net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a sudden drop in lift, which could be interpreted as a change in motion, but it does not explicitly address acceleration as a change in speed and/or direction resulting from a net force. No net force, acceleration, or practical demonstration is described, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: If the wing tilts too steeply, air stops flowing smoothly and lift suddenly drops. This is called a stall!
copy.tl: Kung sobrang taas ng anggulo, hindi na maayos ang daloy ng hangin at biglang nawawala ang lift. Tawag dito ay stall!
copy.bis: Kon sobra ka taas ang anggulo, dili na hapsay ang dagayday sa hangin ug kalit nga mawala ang lift. Gitawag kini og stall!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An adult usually has 4 wisdom teeth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the number of wisdom teeth an adult has. It does not identify or describe any of the digestive system parts listed in the competency (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) nor explain how they work. Wisdom teeth are not among the required parts, so the card provides no direct instructional support.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An adult usually has 4 wisdom teeth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions teeth, which are part of the digestive system, but it does not describe how any human body system works, nor does it address the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems in a meaningful way. It is only tangentially related to the digestive system.

copy.en: An adult usually has 4 wisdom teeth.
copy.tl: Karaniwang may 4 na wisdom teeth (bagang ng katalinuhan) ang isang matanda.
copy.bis: Ang usa ka hamtong kasagaran adunay 4 ka wisdom teeth (bagang sa kaalam).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wood is a renewable fuel because we can always plant new trees to grow and replace the ones we cut!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how increased societal uses of renewable energies could mitigate the effects of global climate change, including how the Philippines could make better use of its plentiful natural resources
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that wood is renewable because trees can be replanted. It does not explain how increased societal uses of renewable energies mitigate climate change, nor does it address the Philippines' use of natural resources. The content is a basic fact about renewable fuel, not direct support for the competency's specific action.

copy.en:
Why is wood considered a renewable fuel?

Wood is a renewable fuel because we can always plant new trees to grow and replace the ones we cut!
copy.tl:
Bakit ang kahoy ay tinatawag na renewable fuel?

Ang kahoy ay isang renewable fuel dahil maaari tayong magtanim ng bagong puno para tumubo at palitan ang mga pinutol!
copy.bis:
Nganong ang kahoy usa ka renewable fuel?

Ang kahoy usa ka renewable fuel kay makatanom ta og bag-ong mga kahoy aron motubo ug mopuli sa mga giputol!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they can lift food heavier than their own body and carry it back to the nest
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ant strength and food carrying but does not mention or describe any outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement or gathering food, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Worker ants are incredibly strong for their size — they can lift food heavier than their own body and carry it back to the nest.
copy.tl: Napakalakas ng mga worker ant kahit maliit sila — kaya nilang buhatin ang pagkaing mas mabigat pa sa sarili nilang katawan at dalhin ito pabalik sa pugad.
copy.bis: Kusgan kaayo ang mga worker ant bisan gamay sila — mabuhat nila ang pagkaon nga mas bug-at pa sa ilang lawas ug dad-on kini balik sa salag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Worker ants are the most numerous in a colony!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about ant colony composition but does not classify living things into groups or use a table as required by the competency. It does not support the skill of classification based on similar characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Worker ants are the most numerous in a colony!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ants but does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a particular habitat. It does not support the competency's requirement of listing examples in a named habitat.

copy.en:
Which ants are most common in a colony?

Worker ants are the most numerous in a colony! There's only one queen but thousands of workers — that's why we see them walking around.
copy.tl:
Sino ang pinakamarami sa kolonya ng langgam?

Ang mga worker ant ang pinakamarami sa kolonya! Isa lang ang reyna, pero libo-libo ang worker — kaya sila ang madalas nating nakikita.
copy.bis:
Kinsay pinakadaghan sa kolonya sa langgam?

Ang mga worker ant ang labing daghan sa kolonya! Usa ra ang reyna, apan liboan ang worker — mao nga sila ang kasagaran natong makita.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The world's first website went online in 1991!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about a science invention (the first website) but does not use information from the home or local community, nor does it explain the invention's impact on everyday life. It only shares a historical fact, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
When did the world's first website go online?

The world's first website went online in 1991! The internet started connecting people a long time ago.
copy.tl:
Kailan naging online ang unang website sa mundo?

Ang unang website sa mundo ay naging online noong 1991! Nagsimula ang internet napakahabang panahon na ang nakalilipas.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a nahimong online ang unang website sa kalibotan?

Ang unang website sa kalibotan nahimong online niadtong 1991! Nagsugod ang internet dugay na kaayo ang milabay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the body fills the gap with collagen, forming a scar
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes wound healing and scar formation via collagen, but does not mention cell division, mitosis, meiosis, or growth. It shares the broad topic of repair but provides no direct instructional support for recognizing the two types of cell division or describing mitosis as growth and repair.

copy.en: When a wound is deep, the body fills the gap with collagen, forming a scar — real skin, but usually without hair or sweat glands.
copy.tl: Kapag malalim ang sugat, pinupunan ng katawan ang butas ng collagen na bumubuo ng peklat — totoong balat ito, pero kadalasang walang buhok o glandula ng pawis.
copy.bis: Kung lawom ang samad, pun-on sa lawas ang lungag og collagen nga maghimo og uwat — tinuod nga panit kini, apan kasagaran walay buhok o glandula sa singot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Once new skin has fully formed underneath, the scab just falls off on its own
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a healing outcome (new skin forming and scab falling off) but does not mention cell division, mitosis, meiosis, or the role of mitosis in growth and repair. It only touches on the general idea of healing, which is related to the competency's context but provides no direct instructional support for the stated skill.

copy.en: Once new skin has fully formed underneath, the scab just falls off on its own — no need to pick at it!
copy.tl: Kapag kumpleto na ang bagong balat sa ilalim, kusang natatanggal ang langib — huwag mong kalkalin!
copy.bis: Kon andam na ang bag-ong panit sa ilalom, ang langib mahulog na lang sa iyaha — ayaw kalkala!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the new tissue that fills it in isn't exactly the same as your original skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains scar formation as a result of new tissue differing from original skin, but it does not mention cell division, mitosis, meiosis, or the role of mitosis in growth and repair. It shares the broad topic of tissue repair but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's specific content.

copy.en:
Why do deep wounds leave a scar?

A deep wound can leave a scar because the new tissue that fills it in isn't exactly the same as your original skin.
copy.tl:
Bakit may peklat sa malalim na sugat?

Kapag malalim ang sugat, minsan naiiwan ang peklat dahil ang bagong tisyung pampuno nito ay hindi kapareho ng dating balat.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga adunay peklat sa lawom nga samad?

Kon lawom ang samad, usahay mabilin kini og peklat tungod kay ang bag-ong unod nga mopuno niini dili parehas sa orihinal nga panit.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s

copy.en: The Wright brothers' very first airplane had a super cool name: it was called the "Wright Flyer"!
copy.tl: Ang unang eroplano ng magkapatid na Wright ay may napakagandang pangalan: tinawag nila itong "Wright Flyer"!
copy.bis: Ang unang eroplano sa magsoon nga Wright adunay nindot nga ngalan: gitawag nila kini nga "Wright Flyer"!

copy.en: A yardang is a long rock ridge carved by wind into a smooth, streamlined shape like the front of a boat!
copy.tl: Ang yardang ay mahabang tagaytay ng bato na inukit ng hangin nang makinis at tulis, parang ilong ng bangka!
copy.bis: Ang yardang usa ka taas nga tagaytay sa bato nga gikulit sa hangin nga hamis ug talinis, sama sa dulong sa sakayan!

copy.bis: Kon mokaon og asukal ang lebadura, mogawas kini og carbon dioxide nga gas nga maghimo og gagmay nga mga burbuha.

copy.tl: Kailangan ng panahon para umalsa ang masa ng tinapay, pinapahinga ito ng panadero nang isang oras o higit pa hanggang halos doble ang laki bago iluto.
copy.bis: Nagkinahanglan og panahon ang minasa aron moalsa, papahuwayon kini sa panadero og usa ka oras o labaw pa hangtod modoble na halos ang gidak-on una lutoon.

copy.en:
What are zeolites and what do they do?

Zeolites are porous minerals with tiny pores for ion exchange! Used in water softeners to remove calcium and magnesium from hard water, and in detergents as phosphate substitutes.
copy.tl:
Ano ang zeolites at ano ang ginagawa nila?

Ang zeolites ay porous minerals na may maliliit na pores para sa ion exchange! Ginagamit sa mga water softener para alisin ang calcium at magnesium sa hard water, at sa mga detergent bilang phosphate substitutes.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang zeolites ug unsa ang ilang buhat?

Ang mga zeolite mga porous mineral nga adunay gagmay nga pores para sa ion exchange! Gigamit sa mga water softener aron tangtangon ang calcium ug magnesium sa hard water, ug sa mga detergent isip phosphate substitutes.
